Palpation of the involved area revealed crepitus consistent with subcutaneous emphysema, and there was 2.5-mm relative proptosis by the Hertel exophthalmometry. There was no other evidence of infectious cellulitis: the involved area was not erythematous, warm, or tender.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 79-year-old man presented with acute-onset, painless swelling around the left eye and cheek six days after zygomatic implant placement. Physical examination revealed marked periocular and facial swelling with crepitus and 2.5-mm proptosis, but no signs of infection. A CT scan confirmed subcutaneous air extending into the left periocular area and orbit, along with a defect in the left maxillary wall adjacent to the dental implant. The subcutaneous emphysema and proptosis resolved spontaneously with observation.
